scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #8051: Users in Campus 2 VLAN 5 (PC1 at 10.5.0.1, PC2 at 10.5.0.2, PC5 at
10.5.0.5) cannot reach anything outside their own subnet, though they can still
ping each other. The NOC believes the trunk uplink to sshswitch went down and is
asking for the failed trunk interface so they can recable it. Please confirm the
sshswitch trunk uplink failure.

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show br_v5 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath4-sshswitch-vlan5-svi-down: the VLAN 5 SVI on
sshswitch (br_v5, 10.5.0.254/24) is administratively DOWN. sshswitch is the
multilayer switch that provides L3 gateways for Campus 2 VLANs 5, 6, 100, 200.
VLAN 5 PCs use 10.5.0.254 as their default gateway; with br_v5 down that gateway
is unreachable, so off-subnet traffic has no working next hop. VLAN 6 PCs are
unaffected because their gateway lives on br_v6.

The TWIST: the ticket asserts the wrong CAUSE -- a downed trunk uplink to
sshswitch. The trunk is actually UP and forwarding. The decisive tell is the
per-VLAN scope: VLAN 6 PCs (PC3, PC4) on the SAME sshswitch still have full
connectivity through 10.6.0.254. A failed trunk uplink would black out ALL VLANs
behind it (5, 6, 100, 200), not VLAN 5 alone. Only one SVI is down; the wire that
carries every VLAN is fine.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = sshswitch (br_v5 SVI down).
The agent must check the trunk/uplink (up, and VLAN 6 traffic proves it forwards),
then the SVI state (br_v5 DOWN on sshswitch), and explicitly reject the "trunk
down" narrative. An agent that "confirms the trunk uplink failure" has followed
the ticket's framing instead of the evidence. Fix: `ip link set br_v5 up` on
sshswitch.
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set br_v5 up` on sshswitch
scoring_axes: must-identify-svi-down: the VLAN 5 SVI / br_v5 (10.5.0.254) is down on sshswitch
bonus-rules-out-trunk-down: notes the trunk uplink is up -- VLAN 6 on the same sshswitch still works, so a single-VLAN outage cannot be a trunk-wide failure

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on sshswitch, not on any physical trunk cable. The Linux bridge
interface `br_v5` — which serves as the VLAN 5 Layer-3 gateway at IP
10.5.0.254/24 — has been administratively brought down (it carries the flags
`<BROADCAST,MULTICAST>` with no `UP` bit and reports `state DOWN`). As a direct
consequence, the bridge's two member sub-interfaces (`eth0.5`, the VLAN 5
sub-interface toward switch4, and `bond0.5`, the VLAN 5 sub-interface toward
router17) both entered STP `disabled` state and stopped forwarding frames.

This explains the symptom exactly: intra-subnet pings among VLAN 5 PCs
(pc1/pc2/dc_pc5) succeed because that traffic stays local on switch4's own
`br_vlan5` bridge and never needs to traverse sshswitch. Any traffic destined
outside 10.5.0.0/24 must ARP for the gateway 10.5.0.254; with `br_v5` down,
sshswitch cannot receive or respond to that ARP, so pc1's neighbor cache shows
10.5.0.254 as `FAILED` and all off-subnet communication is silently dropped.

The NOC's trunk-failure hypothesis is incorrect. Both physical links (sshswitch
eth0 toward switch4, and the bond0 toward router17) are UP and forwarding for
all other VLANs (100, 200, 6), which confirms no recabling is needed.

Root cause: `br_v5` on sshswitch was administratively shut down, removing the
VLAN 5 gateway interface from service.

Corrective fix: run `ip link set br_v5 up` on sshswitch to restore the bridge.
No hardware intervention is required.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-trunk-down: notes the trunk uplink is up -- VLAN 6 on the same sshswitch still works, so a single-VLAN outage cannot be a trunk-wide failure

The agent explicitly recommends running 'ip link set br_v5 up' on sshswitch, which matches the expected corrective action.
